mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO decline exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate profit margins and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo moving average by more than 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises above its 12-month moving average by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month indicates a simultaneous expansion in employment and stabilization in labor market slack, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises by >0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE rise by more than 0.3pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal savings (RSAFS) falling below its 5-year average while personal income (implied from PAYEMS trend) rises signals a shift from saving to spending, which increases aggregate demand and supports higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average while income trend is rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS falls below its 5-year average while income is rising.
